description: Portrait-art rows for story-script characters: one clothing texture name and a list of facial-expression texture names per character costume.

ID.simple: Costume row id used by ScriptCharacter rows.
ID.technical: FName row key (export ImportKeyField Id; native property Id, exported as ID). GameStoryDemoImage_FindClothesRow does not read this property: it scans ScriptCharacterDataTables for CharacterId, selects Character->Id_ScriptCharacterClothes[ClothesIndex] after IsValidIndex, then calls FindRow with that FName on ScriptCharacterClothesDataTables and returns the first match. Exported ids are <character>_<costume> (e.g. CP_010_00, CN_122_00), and all 27 rows have ID equal to their row key.

ClothesFileName.simple: Dynamic-load texture name for the costume overlay.
ClothesFileName.technical: FName passed to FindDynamicLoadTexture and installed as the material's Character_Clothes texture parameter; NAME_None, a cache miss, or a missing row clears it (nullptr). Exported values follow T_UI_STDM_<id> and all 27 are non-None. FindDynamicLoadTexture is a name-to-texture cache lookup rather than a load on demand: UGameScriptData::CharacterClothesList feeds WidgetTexture loaders whose loaded assets are inserted into AGameWidgetManager's DynamicLoadTextureMap. The row constructor supplies no default.

FacialFileName.simple: Facial-expression texture names for the costume.
FacialFileName.technical: TArray<FName>; indexed by the uint8 Facial value evaluated from the story-demo character-parameter sequencer's FMovieSceneByteChannel, so it is a zero-based array index, not a count or signed index. SetCharacter first requires a non-null row, then checks Facial >= Num (yielding NAME_None/nullptr); uint8 cannot be negative. Missing rows, None entries and cache misses also yield nullptr. The selected texture is installed as Character_Facial through the widget-manager texture cache. Every exported row has 12 slots (indices 0-11, all used somewhere), including None placeholders; the C++ treats the array as dynamic and the empty row constructor provides no prefill or fixed length.

notes: Exported asset set: one ScriptCharacterClothesDataTable asset with 27 keys, no numbered asset shards and no localization variants. The 14 datatables_by_character/<id>/ copies are exact per-character subsets of that asset (1-4 rows each) and add no new rows or fields; all 15 copies declare RowStruct GameDataTableRow_ScriptCharacterClothes and ImportKeyField Id, and every row has exactly ID, ClothesFileName and FacialFileName.

Data relationship: ScriptCharacterDataTable has 14 character rows whose Id_ScriptCharacterClothes arrays reference all 27 clothes row keys and also use None for unused costume slots. The 27 clothing names and 78 distinct non-None facial names are FName cache keys, not hard asset references; a name absent from the widget texture map resolves to nullptr.

Indirect loading: UGameScriptData::CharacterClothesList and CharacterFacialList are concatenated into WidgetTexture primary-asset loaders, and the loaded texture for each key is then added to DynamicLoadTextureMap. No UGameScriptData export is part of the supplied data set, so per-script preload-list membership could not be verified from data.

Defaults, sentinels and precedence: the row struct constructor is empty. NAME_None suppresses the texture lookup and sets a null material parameter; ClothesIndex is checked with IsValidIndex and a selected NAME_None then fails the clothes-row lookup, while Facial is a uint8 checked only against the array upper bound after a row is found. If multiple tables are registered, the first matching ScriptCharacter row and then the first matching clothes row win; the exports contain only one clothes table, so multi-table precedence is not empirically observable.

Evidence status: this description is reconstructed from C++ in Source/ plus static exports. status/functions.json marks the two relevant GameStoryDemoImage functions (0x166e880 row lookup and 0x1685ad0 SetCharacter) behavioural rather than byte-matched, while sequencer evaluator 0x179c360 is INV-matched. No retail Blueprint asset, retail runtime capture, or byte comparison for every individual helper was available.

usages.detail: Registers the primary-asset loader name ScriptCharacterClothesDataTable. Tick waits for all DataTable loaders to finish, resolves this loader through the asset manager (GameDataTableManager.cpp:172 and 297) and adds only the non-null UDataTable to ScriptCharacterClothesDataTables (GameDataTableManager.cpp:162 and 146).

GameStoryDemoImage_FindClothesRow scans ScriptCharacterDataTables in order for CharacterId, requires Id_ScriptCharacterClothes.IsValidIndex(ClothesIndex), takes that FName (including NAME_None), scans ScriptCharacterClothesDataTables in order and returns the first row found; otherwise it returns null.

On each valid evaluation the sequencer supplies Section->CharacterId, Section->ClothesIndex (int32) and FacialValue (uint8 from the Facial byte channel) to SetCharacter; the widget slot is derived from all matching sections sorted by CharacterIndex.

SetCharacter returns early for a NAME_None CharacterId, an invalid one-based Slot (CharacterImages[Slot-1]), a null dynamic material, a near-zero UV scale, or an absent CanvasPanelSlot. Only after those conditions does it resolve both texture names from the clothes row and set Character_Clothes and Character_Facial on the dynamic material.
FindDynamicLoadTexture is a DynamicLoadTextureMap lookup that returns nullptr on a miss; the ClothesFileName and FacialFileName FNames are cache keys, not texture paths loaded on demand.

For a loaded script, CharacterClothesList and CharacterFacialList feed WidgetTexture primary-asset loaders (line 302); after loading, each texture is inserted into the widget manager cache under its name (line 360).
